target.title: Equitable partitions of rectangular grid graphs
target.source: Neuberger, Sieben, Swift, Invariant synchrony subspaces of sets of matrices, arXiv:1908.05797 v1/v2; SIAM J. Appl. Dyn. Syst. 19(2) (2020) 964-993, doi:10.1137/19m1283495 (OpenAlex W2967946008)

source_lines.v1: Conjecture 5.6 lines 299-302; remark lines 303-305 ('A direct approach might also work.')
source_lines.v2: Conjecture 5.6 lines 293-294 and 308-309; remark lines 310-313; partition order lines 111-116; Definition 5.1 line 266; Prop 4.5 line 196; trivial-stabilizer remark lines 282-286; McKay example line 276

fixed_meanings.orbit_partition: For H <= Aut(G) acting by h.v = h(v), the partition {Hv}; S1 claims EqPart(G) = {orbit partition of H : H <= Aut(G)} with Aut(G) the full automorphism group.
fixed_meanings.order_direction: Source v2 lines 111-116: A <= B iff A finer; discrete partition is the bottom. EqPart is a subposet (lattice by Prop 4.5). Sub(Aut G) by inclusion. Phi: H -> orbit partition is order-preserving. Under the reverse order the claim would fail for m = n >= 4, since Sub(D4) is not self-dual; the proof uses the correct convention.
fixed_meanings.isomorphic: Both readings are covered: natural Phi is an order isomorphism when a free vertex exists; there is no bijection at all at 2x2 and 3x3.
fixed_meanings.non_injective_phi: Source v2 line 310 notes Z4 and D4 coincide. Independent fibres: at 2x2, 10 subgroups map to 7 partitions (one-class from Z4, Klein {id, rho_r, rho_c, rho_r rho_c} and D4; the diagonal-pair partition from the half-turn group and the diagonal-reflection Klein group); at 3x3, 10 map to 9 (Z4 and D4 only).
fixed_meanings.trivial_stabilizer: Exists v with Stab_{Aut G}(v) = 1, taken in full Aut G; the proof passes from A0 to Aut G through Corollary B (PROOF lines 179-184).
fixed_meanings.exceptions: Free vertex exists iff not 2 <= m = n <= 3; the proof proves both directions, so either reading of 'unless' is covered.

A_statement_fidelity.structure: Three claims: S1 set equality; S2 per-grid equivalence 'EqPart iso Sub(Aut G) iff free vertex'; S3 'free vertex iff not 2<=m=n<=3'. All three are proved, including 'exactly when'.
A_statement_fidelity.degenerate_cases: 1x1 and 1xn are consistent and handled. m = 0 or n = 0 would falsify S2/S3 literally (one-element lattices, no vertex), so m, n >= 1 is implicit in the source and must stay as a hypothesis in Lean (the skeleton has it).
A_statement_fidelity.mathdb_match: The statement is verbatim (\oblong for the box product). Metadata error: the references field and first_stated_year 2018 cite arXiv:1807.10954, which is the unrelated paper 'Domination Mappings into the Hamming Ball' (net/f1/abs1807.html). The first statement is arXiv:1908.05797 v1 (2019). r131 did not note this.
A_statement_fidelity.limitations: The SIADS journal body was not read (paywalled); v2 (Feb 2020) was.

computation.method: Exact split-and-cir enumeration of all equitable partitions (complete DFS over all 2-splits from the coarsest equitable partition; every output re-checked against Definition 5.1), brute force over all set partitions for <= 12 vertices, full Aut(G) by complete backtracking (A0 not assumed), all subgroups by closed-subset enumeration, orbit partitions, Phi injectivity and order-embedding, free-vertex test in full Aut(G).
computation.control: McKay graph (source Fig. 5.1): 8 equitable partitions as the source states, including the non-orbit 124578|36, so the code detects non-orbit partitions.
computation.coverage: 173 grids: 1xn n<=40 and 1x80; 2xn n<=30 and 2x60; 3xn n<=20 and 3x40; 4xn n<=16 and 4x30; all 3<=m<=n<=14; squares 15x15..20x20.
computation.brute_force_cross_checked: 26 grids up to 12 vertices (Bell(12) = 4213597 partitions); all agree with split-and-cir.
computation.results: No non-orbit equitable partition on any grid; Aut G = A0 on every grid; counts 1 / 2 / 5 / 10, with 7 vs 10 at 2x2 and 9 vs 10 at 3x3; a free vertex is absent exactly at 2x2 and 3x3; Phi is an order isomorphism exactly when a free vertex exists.

findings.item: Brito and Manoel, A Symmetry-Based Classification of Synchrony in Tree Networks, J. Nonlinear Sci. 2026, doi:10.1007/s00332-026-10297-1 (OpenAlex W7165152477, abstract only)
findings.impact: Every balanced colouring of a tree is symmetry-induced, so the path case 1xn of S1 is published prior art (also folklore). Missed by r131.

findings.item: Godsil, Compact graphs and equitable partitions, LAA 255 (1997) 259-266; Tinhofer 1991; Wang-Li 2005
findings.impact: Compactness of P_m x P_n would imply S1. No result proving grid compactness was found; recent compact-graph papers (arXiv:2411.09157, arXiv:2606.13928, bodies grepped) do not treat grids. A residual channel, not closed.

findings.item: Krotov, EJC 2023 (arXiv:2010.15839); Svigler-Volek arXiv:2412.21168; Wang-Golubitsky and related lattice papers
findings.impact: Infinite or regular lattices only; no transfer to finite grids with free boundary.
Laplacian brick partitions; not equitable partitions or orbits.

C_prior_art.access: Public HTTP only: arxiv.org abstract and PDF pages, api.openalex.org. No Crossref, Semantic Scholar or arXiv search API. No 403, 429 or challenge responses. OpenAlex returned a shared free-budget notice, so queries were kept few. Receipts are in net/f1..f8/*.receipt.json.
C_prior_art.limitations: Bounded search; the SIADS body, the Brito-Manoel body and the Godsil body were not read.

D_significance.assessment: A genuine resolution of a refereed published conjecture (SIADS 2020), open on MathDB, with no resolution in 15 citing works or the authors' follow-ups; not a wording artefact, parameter instance or source-internal corollary. Modest significance: the path case is known, the automorphism group is classical, the lattice sentence is formal, and the core is about two pages of elementary combinatorics. Credit, if granted, should be framed as S1 for m, n >= 2 with S2 and S3 as consequences.

E_lean_feasibility.statement_assessment: Literal and faithful: pathGraph box product; Setoid equitability; orbitSetoid over Subgroup (G ~g G); HasFreeVertex in full Aut; Setoid order = refinement (matches source); abstract order isomorphism; 1 <= m, n on S2/S3.
required_or_recommended_fixes: Add the natural form: H -> orbitSetoid H is an order isomorphism onto EqPart when a free vertex exists.
Make EqPart an abbrev (instance resolution through a plain def is fragile).
Replace the h-cast A0 definition (fragile) by a subst/case definition or explicit elements.
Fill in map_rel_iff' for rowFlip, colFlip and transpose (easy).
Keep 1 <= m and 1 <= n on S2/S3 (m = 0 falsifies them).
State non-backtracking explicitly in the side-walk lemma; prove degree separation for corner timing.
risky_lemmas: border transitivity for m, n >= 3 (side walks, corner timing, choice of g in A0; suggest a ZMod(2(m+n)-4) border parametrisation)
multiset-subtraction determinism (L2, column and path variants)
transport along the transposition isomorphism and the WLOG conjugations

objections_for_root: Path case 1xn is prior art (Brito-Manoel 2026, trees); exclude it from credit.
Godsil compactness channel: a grid-compactness result would imply S1; none found, not exhaustively excluded.
MathDB metadata error: arXiv:1807.10954 is unrelated; the first statement is arXiv:1908.05797 v1 (2019).
Presentational gaps for the Lean version: non-backtracking walks (PROOF 103-106), WLOG conjugation (113-115), 3x3 corner witnesses (176-177).
Significance is modest (corpus importance, short elementary proof); root weighs it against the substantive-credit standard.
